newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee tumbles, Jan breaches $1,400 mark.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee tumbles, Jan breaches $1,400 mark.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures tumbled to end sharply down, pounded by broad-based selling led by producers amid dwindling roaster buying support.
"There's a bit of dumping around," said one trader.

Traders said the selling gained pace after New York arabica futures slipped after failing to hold onto early gains at the opening. The New York slide followed talk of a possible end to the 11-day truckers' strike in Colombia which some say had hampered coffee shipments.
London's reversal to this week's run-up took the most-active January contract to a session low of $1,375 a tonne after breaking the psychological $1,400 mark.
But some light short-covering and trade buying towards the close helped some prices to cut their losses.
January moved to a high of $1,416 before ending at $1,384, still a $40 loss.
Another said: "The market was due about $40 lower and it really made its due."
Volume at 3,481 lots was rather light and comprised about 350 lots of AAs.
The other interesting feature in the falling market was the strengthening of the Jan/March spread, which widened to a high of $72 at one stage from $47 at Wednesday's close.
"We saw a stronger structure with a falling market," one said.
Options had a rather active day on Thursday with about 750 lots changing hands.
On the physical front, news that Brazil has virtually sold all its 69,000 bags of coffee on offer at an auction was termed by analysts as pretty bullish.
